context: Treemap data visualization showing D3 skill categories sized by line count, with hover tooltips and a legend
first_impression: The structure and layout read clearly, but the leaf cells render as near-black rectangles against the dark background, collapsing the primary color-by-category encoding into visual noise.
what_works: Category label text is well color-coded using a Tol palette and sits cleanly above each group; the title/subtitle/category-label typographic hierarchy is clear and the overall proportions fill the viewport well.
what_doesnt: The fill interpolation (`darker(0.8)` to `brighter(0.3)`) applied to already-dark hues like `#332288` and `#117733` produces fills that are nearly indistinguishable from the `#1a1a2e` body background — the categorical color encoding, the chart's core visual channel, fails for most groups. Cell-level labels are also suppressed for all but the largest cells, leaving most of the treemap as unlabeled dark squares with no recoverable data.
